steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

In a large skillet saute onion in butter or margarine until tender. Remove from heat. Add the bread crumbs, apples, celery, parsley and salt. Mix all together. Cut a large pocket in the side of each pork chop; season inside and out with salt and pepper to taste. Spoon apple mixture loosely into pockets.

In skillet, heat oil to medium high and brown chops on both sides. Place browned chops in an ungreased 9x13 inch baking dish. Cover with aluminum foil and bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes. Remove cover and bake for 30 minutes longer or until juices run clear.

raw_recipe.headline: Apple Stuffed Pork Chops
raw_recipe.description: Thick pork loin chops are heavenly when baked with a simple bread stuffing flavored with apples and celery. The delicious results will look like you've slaved for hours.
raw_recipe.name: Apple Stuffed Pork Chops

review.reviewBody: I have cooked this 2x's now and learned from my mistakes. Two MAJOR CHANGES you need to make. 1.) WAY to much bread crumbs, it was like eating crumbled saltines. Use 2 cups of Apples and 1 cup bread crums. (Recipe wanted 3 cups bread crumbs). 2.) DO NOT cook for 1 hour or it will get too dry. Cook for 20 minutes with foil on and 20 with foil off. With those 2 changes this is a GREAT recipe.

This is an easy recipe that can be easily modified with what you have on hand. I used small cubes of fresh bread instead of fresh bread crumbs and added dried tart cherries in with the apples. I didn’t have celery and didn’t miss it. I only had 1/2” thick pork chops so brown one side of them. Then laid half the chops browned side down in the baking dish, then layered the stuffing on top and then the rest of the chops on top of the stuffing with the browned side up. With the thinner chops, you only need to bake an additional 15 minutes after you remove the foil.

The first time I made this, I followed the recipe exactly, and although we liked it ok, it seemed to lack something. While we were eating, I thought it would be better using packaged stuffing mix and add the sautéed onion & celery, and the diced apples. Well, I've made it at least a dozen times this way, and what a difference! I make Pepperidge Farms herb cubed stuffing per the instructions and add the other things. And no need to transfer to a baking dish if you brown the chops in a cast iron skillet - goes straight into the oven. Huge hit always, and super easy!!!

Just made the stuffing for the pork chops but I did a mini cheat, I bought stovetop, one box for pork and the other cornbread for the flavor but I mixed both stuffings together (1/2 bag of each- only 2 of use - had plenty to stuff and leftovers which I put in an oven safe dish and cooked covered for 20 minutes at 350 ) I did do the recipe as stated but I always put more onion because I love onions. I eliminated the salt because the mixes have enough. The stuffing tastes great. read another's review and took their advice. 20 minutes covered - 20 minutes uncovered. Chops were very moist. THIS ONE IS A KEEPER

Love it. So easy. I did tweak a bit. Only used 1 cup of bread crumbs and also added cranberries. I also dipped stuffed chops in egg and Panko and pan fried about 2 mins on each side. Put in oven covered with foil 20 minutes and uncovered 20 minutes. Very juicy and cooked perfectly. Will be adding this to the rotation.

I gave this recipe 4 stars because I did not follow the recipe exactly, but it turned out DELICIOUS! I used some suggestions from other reviews. With the onion and butter, I added garlic salt, poultry seasoning and 3-4 slices of bacon cut up. I also only added about 3/4 cup of bread crumbs and a sleeve of ritz crackers crumbled up with apple juice added for good moisture. I did not stuff the chops because I knew my kids wouldn't like it, so I browned the chops (with oil and salt and pepper) and put them on top of the stuffing in the pan, poured some more apple juice on top and cooked as instructed. Towards the end I made sure to mix some of the stuffing mix on top of the pork chops so they would be nicely flavored. Excellent!

I too found it wonderful with the recommended changes. Also added a clove of garlic to the cornbread stuffing along with half a dozen cranraisins,; stuffed the chops and wrapped bacon around the circumference pinning with a tooth pick. 30 min's covered, 13 mins. uncovered. Oh, the gravy is ta die for.

My husband and I thought this recipe was great! I did increase the apples, added a little more celery, added 1 Tbsp of apple juice, 2 Tbsp of buttermilk and 1/4 C of chopped walnuts. There was extra stuffing, so I put it on top of and around the chops. I sprinkled them with a few pinches of cinnamon and baked it 20 minutes with foil and then 20 minutes without. I'm keeping this in my recipe arsenal for sure!

I made a rub of paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, oregano, salt and pepper and put on it. 20 min covered and then 20 min uncovered. Cut way back on the bread crumbs. After all the changes was so moist and yummy. Will make again.
I added some fresh Rosemary & Thyme. It turned out great and the meat was very moist. I used "bone in" chops for added flavor, folded them over the stuffing and secured with toothpicks. Enjoy

This is my second time making this dish and it's delicious and easy. Got a good browned chop with my cast iron skillet, transferred to 9x13 and covered it with foil and transferred to the oven. Used old bread (loaf, hotdog buns) for the crumbs. Removed the pork chops after cooking and added juices and cream to cast iron to deglaze browned bits and make a pan sauce. Economical, too!
This was delicious. Will make again

So, I had a bit of an adventure in the kitchen tonight with those stuffed chops. I was really hopeful, but I have to admit, they didn't quite turn out as planned. The meat somehow ended up on the dry side, and I was scratching my head because it seemed to lose all its flavor in the process. And the stuffing, bless its heart, just went completely soggy! It's so funny because I followed the recipe exactly, step by step, so I'm honestly not sure what happened there. Guess some nights, even the best intentions lead to... well, a memorable meal for other reasons! Haha.
My family absolutely loved this recipe! It definitely made the same old boring chicken lively and delicious! Even my teenager loved it! We definitely recommend!

we really enjoyed with the suggestions made. A bit more onion, only a cup of bread crumbs, and baked probably 40 minutes until temp registered done. Spooned over drippings. Mixed chicken broth and dabs of butter over extra dressing and baked. Might add pecans next time.
Just added some spice with the apple mixture otherwise all good ty
cut down bread crumbs & brined the pork chops in apple juice & spices per others suggestions. Found a use for my brown sugar glaze that has been languishing in the fridge! Yay!
